pages.text: "Mr. Pig, watch me! I'm so fast!" Coco raced around the kitchen. Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks, set one down with a thump. Spilled flour lay white as snow on the floor.

"The faster I run, the more fun! All the way in one go!" Coco ran toward the oven, the big fiery place where bread bakes. Its door was hot. Mom shouted, "Coco, don't run!" But Coco was already far ahead.

Then Coco's feet slipped across the floury floor! Thump! Coco landed on their bottom, with their front paws stopping right before the oven door. Their tail went stiff. "Oh—ah!" Coco had almost been burned.
Mom quickly lifted Coco up. "Are you okay? Running feet don't stop easily." Coco nodded. "I didn't know the floor was slippery..." Mom held their paw. "Shall we learn our kitchen promises?"
Mom pointed at the floor. Coco's slide had left a long mark in the flour. It ended right at the oven door. "See? Running sends you sliding all the way here." Coco looked and pressed their lips shut.
Mom counted them one by one. "One, walk in the kitchen! Two, gently on the floury floor! Three, stay three steps back from the oven!" Coco tried gentle steps on their toes. "By the oven, walk!"
This time Coco held the bread basket and walked lightly. Gently on the floury floor, and three steps back from the oven. "By the oven, walk!" Mr. Pig took the basket.
Coco stood proud. "Walking means I don't slip at all!" Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. Mr. Pig nodded. "Now you're better at this than I am!"
Now Coco kept the three kitchen promises alone. "One, walk! Two, gently on the floury floor! Three, three steps back from the oven!" When Mr. Pig came again, Coco called first, "By the oven, walk!"
That evening, Mom wrapped her floury arms around Coco's back. By the oven, walking feet are braver than running feet. Coco buried their face in Mom's apron. "By the oven, walk!"
